2608.16804.title: Cross-Sign Language Transfer Learning Using Domain Adaptation with Multi-scale Temporal Alignment
2608.16804.paper_summary: Sign language serves as a vital means of communication for individuals with hearing impairments, yet recognition resources for the over 100 distinct sign languages are severely lacking. In response, we present our work on sign language recognition using transfer learning and the domain adaptation method TA3N, which utilizes the Temporal Relational Network (TRN) module for aligning multi-scale temporal relations. Our findings highlight the superior performance of Domain Adaptation to neural network-based transfer learning, particularly in improving recognition of American Sign Language (ASL). Our research also identifies the effectiveness of aligning shorter-term temporal features between source and target domains. In addition to using RGB, we conducted experiments using Optical Flow mode for the sign language samples, ultimately determining that RGB outperforms Optical Flow in the majority of cases. Our work aims to improve accessibility and communication for individuals who rely on sign language as their primary mode of communication.
2608.16804.paper_summary_zh: 手語對於聽障人士而言是一種重要的溝通方式，但對於超過100種不同手語的識別資源卻嚴重不足。為此，我們提出了使用轉移學習和領域適應方法TA3N的手語識別工作，該方法利用時間關係網絡（TRN）模塊來對齊多尺度的時間關係。我們的研究結果突顯了領域適應在基於神經網絡的轉移學習中的優越性能，特別是在改善美國手語（ASL）的識別方面。我們的研究還確定了在源域和目標域之間對齊短期時間特徵的有效性。除了使用RGB外，我們還對手語樣本進行了使用光流模式的實驗，最終確定在大多數情況下，RGB的表現優於光流。我們的工作旨在改善依賴手語作為主要溝通方式的個體的可及性和溝通能力。
